title: Daily Dashboard
tagline: A morning dashboard: spending by category, recurring subscriptions, weather and today's calendar.
highlights: Pulls bank transactions through SimpleFIN Bridge, chosen over Plaid because Plaid bills per API call
Homegrown transaction categorizer and recurring-charge detector, since SimpleFIN provides neither
A daily job writes JSON snapshots and the API serves from cache, so pages load instantly and stay under rate limits
Receipt scanning with local OCR; manual entries reconcile automatically once the bank transaction posts
role: Solo: API, data pipeline, frontend, deployment
problem: Checking spending meant opening a bank app, weather meant another app, and my calendar a third. I wanted one page I open each morning that answers "how am I doing this week?" without paying per API call or waiting on slow APIs every load.

challenges.title: Bank data on a personal budget
challenges.body: Plaid bills per API call, which adds up for a dashboard refreshed daily. SimpleFIN Bridge costs a flat ~$15 a year but returns raw descriptions only, so I wrote the categorizer and the recurring-charge detector myself.

challenges.title: Fast pages over slow APIs
challenges.body: A systemd timer runs one refresh job a day that calls SimpleFIN, NWS and Google Calendar and writes JSON snapshots. The API only reads those snapshots, so the page loads instantly and never hits rate limits.

challenges.title: Bank data lags reality
challenges.body: You can type in a purchase or scan a receipt (local Tesseract OCR plus regex parsing) and it counts right away. When the real transaction posts with the same amount within 3 days, the manual entry reconciles itself away so nothing is double-counted.
